Android lets an equalizer attach to an app\'s audio only if that app announces it, or to everything at once – the global mix – if the device permits. Pegel cannot hear or change audio in any other way. That is why it works with some apps and not with others.

1. Switch Pegel on first, then close the player completely and open it again.
2. Check the line at the top of the Sound tab: it names what Pegel is attached to.
3. Try another connection mode in Settings.
4. Switch off other equalizers, including the one built into your phone or player, and restart the phone.

Some players only announce themselves when asked to:
• Poweramp: enable MusicFX in the advanced tweaks and on the equalizer page.
• VLC: set the audio output to AudioTrack.
• Musicolet: Settings › Audio › System equalizer.
• Neutron: enable “DSP Effect (Device)”.
• BlackPlayer: Audio › Equalizer › Default equalizer.
• Deezer: enable the equalizer in the sound settings.
Menu names change between versions – look for “system equalizer”.

Apps that neither announce their audio nor play through the global mix stay untouched – typically apps with their own audio engine or copy protection. If neither Automatic nor Global mix only changes the sound, no equalizer app can do it on this device without root.

If the sound changes on the speaker but not over Bluetooth, the phone hands the audio to the Bluetooth chip before effects are applied. In the developer options, turn on “Disable Bluetooth A2DP hardware offload” and restart. With USB DACs that play bit-perfect, effects are bypassed by design.
Some phones stop background apps aggressively. Exempt Pegel from battery optimisation in Settings › Running, and allow it to run in the background in your phone\'s own battery settings.
It gets quieter, distorts or pumps

A boost cannot go above full scale. Pegel therefore lowers the whole level by the largest boost of equalizer and bass – the status card says by how much. That is why a boosted sound is quieter than a flat one; turn the volume up to compensate, or cut bands instead of boosting others.\n\nLoudness is the exception: it pushes the level against a limiter on purpose. High values make the volume move in waves with the beat – take it back if you hear that.

Pegel still names a player that is closed

A player that is closed by force never tells Pegel that it stopped, and Android does not report it either. Pegel then stays attached to nothing. Tap “Detach” in the line at the top of the Sound tab to return to the global mix; the player is followed again the next time it announces itself.

Where the suggested sound comes from

For headphones Pegel ships corrections from the AutoEq project: about 6,000 models, each measured by someone and turned into a curve for Pegel\'s ten bands. Pegel recognises headphones by their Bluetooth name; if yours are named differently, search the model.\n\nFor speakers, cars and the phone\'s own speaker nobody publishes such measurements. There Pegel offers its own starting curve for the kind of device – a sensible start, not a measurement. Every suggestion becomes a normal profile that you can change or delete.

Galaxy phones bring their own sound effects (Settings › Sounds and vibration › Sound quality and effects: Dolby Atmos, Equalizer, Adapt Sound). They work in addition to Pegel. If it sounds doubled, harsh or distorted, switch them off there and let Pegel do the shaping alone.
Headphone corrections come from AutoEq by Jaakko Pasanen, built on measurements by oratory1990, crinacle, Rtings and others.
